comments.author: @enriquegonzalez9017
comments.text:
Im 32 now and  have been cutting since i was 16, and the best way to explain the waves we get go like this. 

January starts off slow because everyone is broke after Christmas,new years and paying taxes if you have to pay.
It starts picking up towards mid February people start geting their tax refunds and guess what now you have valentines day right around the corner both those thing bring in the clients.
Then it stays steady untill BOOM kids get out of school and now parents dont have to cut their kids hair for atleast 1 or 2 month because that extra money is going toward daycare or extra food since kids are home more. AND thats when everyone starts going on vacation so even more broke thru summer.

Picks up again the week before and after the first day of school for back to school haircuts but from buying new cloths, supplies, exc. For back to school parents are broke again so It can get slow couple weeks into back to school.

End of month week is also usaully  slowest week every month since everyone has to pay rent.

The rest of the year just comes in waves stimulated by the holidays, big concerts and sport events. Ive been owning my own shop since i was 21 hope this helps. 

And before i finish we charge $35 just haircut and $40 inludes beard in the Dallas area. At the end of the day you keep it affordable so people can come in couple times a month. Its hard to get regular clients but its really easy to lose them just remember that when you want to raise prices more than $10 in a single year i have always increased by $5 and kept i wanna say 95% of the clients.
